hints: For a system of coplanar forces in equilibrium, the algebraic sum of resolved components along any two perpendicular directions must each equal zero: $\Sigma F_x = 0$ and $\Sigma F_y = 0$.
Resolve forces vertically first so that the horizontal $10\text{ N}$ force does not enter the equation: $2P\sin\theta = P\sin 60^\circ$.
Divide both sides by $P$ to obtain $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}\sin 60^\circ$, and solve for $\theta$.
Resolve forces horizontally: $2P\cos\theta + P\cos 60^\circ = 10$, substitute your value of $\theta$, and solve for $P$.
walkthrough:
Since the coplanar forces are in equilibrium, the algebraic sum of the vertical components must equal zero:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies 2P\sin\theta - P\sin 60^\circ = 0$$
$$2P\sin\theta = P\sin 60^\circ$$

Divide both sides by $P$ (since $P > 0$) to solve for $\theta$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{\sin 60^\circ}{2} = \frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \approx 0.43301$$
$$\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.43301) \approx 25.7^\circ$$

Resolve forces horizontally and set the sum equal to zero:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies 2P\cos\theta + P\cos 60^\circ = 10$$
$$P(2\cos\theta + \cos 60^\circ) = 10$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the conditions for static equilibrium of coplanar forces:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \Sigma F_y = 0$$
The sum of components in any chosen orthogonal directions must vanish.

Resolve forces perpendicular to the $10\text{ N}$ horizontal force (vertically), taking the upward direction as positive:
$$2P\sin\theta - P\sin 60^\circ = 0$$
Add $P\sin 60^\circ$ to both sides:
$$2P\sin\theta = P\sin 60^\circ$$

Divide both sides by the non-zero force magnitude $P$:
$$2\sin\theta = \sin 60^\circ$$
Substitute $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866025$:
$$2\sin\theta = 0.866025$$
Divide both sides by $2$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{0.866025}{2} = 0.433013$$
Apply the inverse sine function:
$$\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.433013) = 25.6589^\circ \approx 25.7^\circ$$

Resolve forces parallel to the $10\text{ N}$ horizontal force, taking the direction opposing the $10\text{ N}$ force as positive:
$$2P\cos\theta + P\cos 60^\circ - 10 = 0$$
Add $10$ to both sides and factor out $P$:
$$P(2\cos\theta + \cos 60^\circ) = 10$$

Substitute the unrounded angle $\theta = 25.6589^\circ$ and $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$:
$$\cos 25.6589^\circ \approx 0.901388$$
$$P(2 \times 0.901388 + 0.5) = 10$$
$$P(1.802776 + 0.5) = 10$$
$$2.302776 P = 10$$
Divide both sides by $2.302776$:
$$P = \frac{10}{2.302776} \approx 4.3426 \approx 4.34\text{ N}$$
